items.title: Govt stalls Alipay+ tie-up over data security concerns
items.description: Alipay+'s proposal to link with India's payment system faces national security concerns.  Concerns also exist regarding the storage and use of customer data.  This proposal was the first from a China-linked entity in the financial sector.  India and China are working to maintain peace at the border.  Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit is expected to stabilize bilateral relations.

items.title: Canara Bank eyes $2 billion overseas bond raise
items.description: Canara Bank plans to raise up to $2 billion from overseas markets under its MTN programme, with the funds to be mobilised through its GIFT City or other overseas branches.

items.title: Sebi set to review derivative settlement prices amid concerns over CAS
items.description: Sebi will review derivative settlement price methods.  This follows market participant feedback after the new closing auction session.  The regulator introduced the closing auction session in the equity cash segment.  This session determines the closing price of securities for derivatives.  A consultation paper on proposed changes will be issued soon.

items.title: FPIs pump Rs 13,010 crore into Indian equities in second half of August
items.description: Overseas investors continued buying Indian equities for five straight fortnights. They invested over thirteen thousand crore rupees in the latter half of August. Consumer services, financials, and healthcare sectors received significant foreign portfolio inflows. Capital goods also saw renewed investor interest after previous outflows. Oil, gas, and consumable fuels experienced the largest foreign investment outflows.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Domestic equities closed mixed as the Nifty saw a slight decline. Elevated crude oil prices are keeping investor sentiment cautious in the market. Foreign portfolio investors were net sellers, while domestic investors bought shares. The Indian Rupee continued its gaining momentum against the US dollar. Several stocks are currently under the F&O ban period.

items.title: Stocks in news: HDFC Bank, M&M, Gland Pharma, CreditAccess Grameen and Bharat Forge
items.description: Indian benchmark indices extended their losing streak for a fourth consecutive session on Thursday.  Nifty 50 fell 0.17% and Sensex declined 0.55% amid market pressures.  HDFC Bank raised nearly $12 billion through Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits.  Mahindra & Mahindra expects truck business integration by January and electric bus launch by April.  Fosun Pharma is likely to divest a 5% stake in Gland Pharma through a block deal.

items.title: NSE’s mega IPO moves closer as SC approves Sebi settlement
items.description: In a pivotal decision, the Supreme Court has validated the National Stock Exchange’s settlement concerning the co-location and dark fibre matters. This marks a crucial step forward as the exchange readies for its initial public offering, expected to attract nearly thirty-one thousand crore rupees. Once completed, this IPO could become the second-largest in the nation, following the regulatory body’s acceptance of the significant settlement payment.

items.title: These large- and mid-cap stocks can give more than 20% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: The Indian market was under pressure on Thursday, particularly at the index level. Rising crude-oil prices are an obvious concern, but domestic factors like selling and market repricing in select sectors may also be beginning to impact sentiment. Also, are there early indications that Indian equities will be charting their own course as compared to what is happening in the global markets?

items.title: Banks offer semi-fixed loans to deploy surplus liquidity
items.description: Banks are deploying surplus liquidity through new mortgage products.  HSBC and Kotak Mahindra Bank lead with semi-fixed home loan options.  These products offer fixed rates for a period before switching.  This strategy aims to protect lending margins amid interest rate uncertainty.  Surplus funds are also being considered for government securities.

items.title: LCR reset creates ₹2.1 Lakh-crore lending headroom for PSU Banks
items.description: Public sector banks gained significant lending headroom after liquidity requirement relaxation. This allows them to sustain credit growth while deposit mobilisation remains relatively weak. Excess investment buffers could support incremental loan growth on their substantial loan books. Banks can now free up funds tied up in government bonds for lending. This improvement is visible at some of the largest state-owned lenders.
